title: Aurum Alpha browser bootstrap document
description: What the origin that served the bundle tells the client, rendered from THAT origin's environment. Governed by standards/web-client.md WC2. Deliberately minimal: it exists to solve the ordering problem that the client cannot ask the API where the API is. Everything the backend knows about itself belongs on GET /api/config, and the frontend's own build provenance is compiled into the bundle — no server can supply it, because under a split origin the backend has no idea which frontend build a given browser is running. Served to every anonymous visitor and therefore PUBLIC BY CONSTRUCTION. schemaVersion 2 — see the schema_version note.

schema_version.description: Version 1 carried a 'build' object and required it. That was wrong: build provenance describes the frontend artifact and is compiled in by the bundler, so a serving origin cannot supply it. Removing a required field is breaking under PC6 and so takes a new version; the deprecation window is nil because no implementation consumed version 1 — stated rather than assumed.

environment.description: Which environment served this bundle. The bundle is identical across all of them (WC2); this is how the running client knows where it landed.

api_base_url.description: Origin the API client (WC3) calls. Under WC1 the browser sends a session cookie and no Authorization header, so this is an origin that cookie is scoped to and no cross-origin credential handling arises.

auth.description: Where the client sends a user to begin and end a session. Deliberately just two paths: under WC1 the browser's behaviour is identical whichever authentication architecture is in place, so it is not told which one that is. The architecture belongs to the authentication and authorization standard.

login_path.description: Path the client navigates to in order to begin a login. A top-level navigation, not a fetch — the OIDC provider must be able to render its own UI and redirect back.

logout_path.description: Path that ends the session. Ending it is the server's job, not the page's: the session's real state lives server-side and the browser cannot revoke it by discarding anything it holds (WC1).

features.description: Per-environment toggles the client reads at load. Present so that a toggle is never a reason to rebuild the bundle, which is the WC2 failure this document exists to prevent. The evaluation contract itself belongs to the feature flags standard, not here.
